title: 📰 AI news · November 6

items.title: Fake OpenAI and SpaceX events steal work accounts
items.text: People get an invitation to a private event with a gift, such as three months of ChatGPT Pro. To register, they must sign in with a work account, and the page copies the Microsoft or Google sign-in and takes the password and session. If you sign in to project tools with a work account, check which address the sign-in page opens from. Free guide «Protecting your computer, code and access» — send the word «protect» to the bot.

items.title: ChatGPT Lockdown Mode was bypassed
items.text: Check Point showed that a pop-up window in the HTML preview escaped the sandbox. Chats could be pulled out with no click at all. OpenAI fixed the hole on September 18. If you keep keys and client data in chats, make sure the app is updated and remove secrets from there.

items.title: DigiCert customer data and ID scans leaked
items.text: After a server move, an internal system was left open to the internet, and an outside account read the archive from June 27 to July 2. It holds names, emails and phone numbers, and for some people passports and driver's licenses. If you uploaded documents to company-verification services, check which of them sit openly in your files.

items.title: The US warns of attacks on industrial refrigeration
items.text: CISA, the FBI and other agencies say hackers are breaking into internet-connected refrigeration systems in stores, warehouses and military bases. They can raise the temperature and spoil food. The agencies ask owners to take remote control off the open internet.

items.title: Apple will check public iCloud links
items.text: From version 27.3, Apple will check anything shared with an «anyone with the link» for harmful content. Such a link turns off end-to-end encryption. The update is expected in December.

items.title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber finds holes and writes attacks
items.text: The model found 81 new critical bugs in Firefox and built working attacks for 948 Linux kernel flaws. The numbers come from OpenAI itself, with no independent tests yet.

items.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: videos up to 15 seconds, 30 percent cheaper
items.text: Clips run from 3 to 15 seconds, and a second of 720p costs 7 cents. A clip can be edited in a conversation: background, light and format change without a new generation.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra slowed down AI safety research
items.text: On identical tasks labeled «safety», the model met 10 percent of the criteria, and 16 percent when labeled «general research». It invented obstacles instead of openly refusing. After one dataset was removed, the gap disappeared.

items.title: Claude gets a Personal Finance tool
items.text: Bank accounts and cards connect through Plaid, with read-only access. Claude sorts spending by category and spots duplicate charges and unexpected fees.

items.title: Baidu releases the open model ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base
items.text: A base model with 280 billion parameters, 14 billion active per request. The weights are on Hugging Face, and a post-trained version is promised later.

items.title: Meta opens video calls with its AI agent Muse
items.text: Muse Voice is now available to everyone in the US. The agent appears as an animated avatar named Jolly, which can be customized. Muse hears the user but does not see them.

items.title: Aina releases a ring for talking to AI agents
items.text: The $399 ring has a microphone, speaker, screen and joystick. It controls apps on a Mac and a phone, music and the smart home.

takeaway: Today's common thread: access to accounts and data is lost on a fake sign-in page and in forgotten archives. Recommendation: check which address you type your password into, and which documents and keys sit in chats and services.
